literal: Help extent-it-is is-not help; help done-they-who-received of-nobility extent-it-is.
translation: The value of a help is not measured by the extent of the help itself. It is measured by the nobility of those who received it.
modern: ஒருவருக்குச் செய்யும் உதவியின் மதிப்பு, அந்த உதவியின் அளவைப் பொறுத்தது அன்று. அது அந்த உதவியைப் பெற்றவர்களின் நற்பண்பின் அளவைப் பொறுத்தது.
explanation: This couplet explains how to measure the true worth of a good deed. The word 'உதவி' (help) is repeated to contrast the physical act of helping with its ultimate value. The extent ('வரைத்து') of a benefit is not determined by the material size of the help given. Instead, its true measure corresponds to the 'சால்பு' (nobility or worthiness) of the person who receives it, as a noble person will value even a small help immensely.
